what_it_does: TEGRA is a system architecture for processing large graph data by separating computation and memory resources rather than tightly coupling them together. Graphs are data structures with nodes connected by edges, common in social networks and recommendation systems. When some workloads need more computing power while others need more memory access bandwidth, traditional designs waste resources. TEGRA uses disaggregated memory accessed over CXL (a high-speed connection standard for linking memory to distant processors) and message-passing communication to dynamically match compute and memory resources to workload needs.
